newsitem.title: USA: Florida stop sign convictions will be appealed.
newsitem.headline: Florida stop sign convictions will be appealed.

text.p: The conviction of three people found guilty of manslaughter for removing a stop sign from an intersection where three teenagers died in a crash will be appealed, a lawyer for one of the convicts said Thursday.
A jury deliberated for about four hours before finding Nissa Baillie, 21, Thomas Miller, 20, and Christopher Cole, 20, all of Mulberry, Fla., guilty late Wednesday of manslaughter and grand theft.
The three admitted stealing stop signs at other intersections for fun but denied stealing the one at the intersection where the three teenagers died on Feb. 7, 1996.
Joe Episcopo, attorney for one of the defendants, called the verdicts "a miscarriage of justice" and said an appeal would be filed.
"It's going to result in a very heavy prison sentence for these kids, and it will have to be corrected by the appellate courts," he said.
The case stemmed from a stop sign that was missing from a busy intersection in Valrico, a Tampa suburb.
A car driven by Kevin Farr, and carrying his friends Brian Hernandez and Randall White, all 18, crossed the intersection and was struck by a tractor-trailer truck. All three died instantly.
Episcopo said there was "insufficient circumstantial evidence for a conviction."
The jury heard conflicting testimony during a three-week trial. The three accused teens admitted stealing signs, but said they did not take the one at the fatal intersection.

Robert Fulks, of Plant City, Florida, testified the day before the crash he saw a semi-trailer truck backing up toward the sign. Later, when he passed through the intersection again, he said the stop sign was down.
Under Florida law the manslaughter and grand theft convictions carry possible prison terms totalling 46 years.
Circuit Judge Bob Anderson Mitcham set sentencing for June 19.
